title: Chapter 5.  Constitutional Status — A Union Territory WITH a Legislative Assembly

blocks.content: Puducherry's most important polity fact is structural: unlike most Union Territories, it has its own elected Legislative Assembly and Chief Minister, placing it in a small, exclusive category alongside Delhi and (since 2019) Jammu and Kashmir.

Puducherry's Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers are established under Article 239A of the Constitution of India (inserted by the Constitution (Fourteenth Amendment) Act, 1962, enacted specifically to enable Parliament to create legislatures and Councils of Ministers for certain Union Territories), read together with the Government of Union Territory of Pondicherry Act, 1962.

Unlike Delhi's special Article 239AA framework (created much later, by the 69th Amendment in 1991, and involving a more complex, frequently litigated division of powers with the Lieutenant Governor, as detailed in the companion Delhi GS volume), Puducherry's Article 239A framework is comparatively simpler and older, and — notably — Parliament retains full discretion under Article 239A over whether to have a Legislature for a UT at all, and could in principle modify or withdraw it (a structural difference from Delhi's more entrenched, litigation-tested special status).

Puducherry's Legislative Assembly can legislate on matters in the State List and Concurrent List (subject to the overall constitutional scheme for Union Territories), but — as with any UT legislature — Parliament retains overriding concurrent legislative power for the territory, and the Administrator/Lieutenant Governor retains specified reserved powers and a role in reserving certain bills for Presidential consideration.

cells: Government of Union Territory of Pondicherry Act, 1962
30 elected seats + up to 3 nominated members (33 total)
Lieutenant Governor, appointed by the President of India
Chief Minister, appointed by the LG based on ability to command confidence of the Assembly

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Puducherry, Delhi and Jammu & Kashmir are the ONLY THREE Union Territories with a Legislative Assembly and Chief Minister — a frequently tested comparative list also covered in the companion Delhi and J&K GS volumes. Puducherry's enabling provision (Article 239A, 1962) is the OLDEST of the three; Delhi's (Article 239AA) came in 1991; J&K's UT-with-Assembly status dates only to 2019-2024.

items: Puducherry's Assembly is notable for allowing up to 3 members to be NOMINATED (rather than directly elected) by the Central Government — these nominated members enjoy the same voting rights as elected members on most matters, a distinctive feature not found in most other Indian legislatures.

This nomination provision has, at various points in Puducherry's political history, become significant and even politically decisive in closely contested Assembly arithmetic, since nominated members' votes can affect government formation or survival in a small, 30-elected-seat Assembly — a distinctive feature that has occasionally generated litigation and political controversy over the years regarding the timing and manner of such nominations.

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Puducherry's UP TO 3 NOMINATED Assembly members (with full voting rights on most matters) is a distinctive and frequently tested feature — remember this is a notably higher proportion relative to the Assembly's small 30-elected-seat size than nomination provisions found in most other Indian legislatures.

items: Puducherry, Delhi, and J&K = the only 3 UTs with a Legislative Assembly + Chief Minister.
Puducherry's Assembly: Article 239A (1962) — the OLDEST such provision among the three (Delhi: 1991; J&K: 2019-2024).
30 elected seats + up to 3 nominated members (33 total); nominated members have full voting rights on most matters.
Head of UT: Lieutenant Governor; Head of Government: Chief Minister.
